correctness.rationale: An exact p-integral product and power binomial expansion yield F_m(q+p^kt)=F_m(q)+p^kt mod p^(k+1) for every prime p, k>=1. Base F_m(q)=0 modp, then one root per residue at every lift. PNT in fixed arithmetic progressions yields the exact prime density; finite checks do not substitute for proof.

value.rationale: The natural parameter-dual question asks how many prime bases satisfy each fixed prime-power congruence. A full exact answer for every prime power, including p=2,3, together with a positive explicit prime-base density and an exact p-adic unit-slope lemma is structurally motivated and not merely a numerical instance.
